result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. Three items were correct, two partial and one wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only writes a request naming the tool and its arguments. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You picked "it will eventually fix the bug". An agent repeating the same failing step needs a stopping condition, such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | 4 is the right count. Your reasoning said the model runs the tools itself, but the program runs them. That is why each result needs another model call. |
| q5 | correct | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide what to do next. |
| q6 | partial | The name is part of it, but the model also relies on each tool's description and parameters. |

**Summary:** You have the loop and the model's role in tool calling mostly down, and it held up four days later. Two things need work. The model only asks for tools and the program runs them. A loop also needs a stopping condition.

**Next step:** Write a one-sentence description for `check_calendar`, with its parameters. Then write what stops the loop if the calendar tool keeps returning errors. That covers all three gaps, and it comes before the context and memory lessons.

I also added learning record 0003 and updated `NOTES.md`. `s1` is still ungraded.
